clue.text: Member of literary club is in the papers

definitions.text: Member of literary club is in the papers

parts.words: Member of literary club is in the papers
parts.note: a member of the club founded by Dickens's genial hero, who appears throughout the novel whose title calls itself a set of Papers

explanation.surface: A member of a book club has made the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the papers' looks like the press, but it is the title of Dickens's first novel, The Pickwick Papers, in which the club and its members appear.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective-turned-noun names a member of the Dickensian club in that novel.

clue.text: Almost pledge hand

indicators.note: almost means the word for pledge is taken without its final letter

parts.note: to pawn something is to pledge it as security

explanation.surface: Someone nearly promises their hand in marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter, N, from PAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's foot, and informally a person's hand, is called this.

clue.text: Game that never starts 0-0?

parts.note: 0-0 looks like a goalless football score, but it is the notation for castling on the king's side, a move never possible as the opening move

explanation.surface: A match that can never kick off goalless.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess notation 0-0 records kingside castling, which needs pieces to have moved out of the way first, so no game begins with it.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game of kings and queens is recorded in notation where 0-0 means castling.

clue.text: Lacking humour, you got taken in

indicators.note: the word for you got taken in, so it sits inside the word for humour

parts.note: wit is humour
thou is the old word for you

explanation.surface: Someone without a sense of humour has been fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got taken in' is the container signal; 'Lacking humour' looks like one phrase, but the definition is the single word 'Lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition it means lacking or minus something.

clue.text: In his sport he can follow initial score with a couple, but not a pair

definitions.text: In his sport he can follow initial score with a couple, but not a pair

parts.words: In his sport he can follow initial score with a couple, but not a pair
parts.note: a batsman out for nothing in his first innings may make two runs in his second, but must avoid a second nought, the dreaded pair

explanation.surface: A player may add two to his opening score, but not a matched set.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pair' in cricket is being out for nought in both innings of a match, so 'a couple' (two runs) and 'a pair' differ here though they look like the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the bat-and-ball game where a pair means two ducks.

clue.text: Block being entered in the wrong order

indicators.note: in the wrong order means the two halves of the phrase for being entered swap places

parts.note: got in means was entered, as a place is

explanation.surface: Something gets blocked because it was typed in the wrong sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wrong order' swaps GOT IN round to IN GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of cast metal, such as gold, is a solid block.

clue.text: Have little complaint in police station about tip-off

indicators.note: the word for police station goes about the other letters, wrapping them

parts.note: nick is British slang for a police station

indicators.note: off means the letters of tip are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone at the station grumbles about being tipped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles TIP to TPI, which 'about' places within the British slang word for a police station (it can also mean prison).
explanation.definitionFit: To quibble is to make petty, small objections.

clue.text: Shoot mate in America

definitions.meaning: a young growth on a plant
American slang for a friend, short for buddy

explanation.definitionFit: Both the plant's new growth and the American word for a pal share this spelling.

clue.text: Astronomical curiosity discovered in Calcutta

definitions.meaning: a collapsed star whose gravity lets no light escape
the notorious cramped prison cell in Calcutta of 1756

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a region of space from which light cannot escape and the infamous cell of Calcutta.

clue.text: Understanding cistern, mend break

indicators.note: break means the letters of cistern and mend are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A plumber shows know-how by fixing a broken water tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' shuffles CISTERN and MEND together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Good judgement or insight is synonymous with understanding.

clue.text: Tearing off round lake for sport

indicators.note: round means the word for tearing off goes round the letter for lake

parts.note: wresting is pulling or tearing something away
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone tears around a lake for exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts WRESTING round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappling contests between two combatants form a sport.

clue.text: Opera for orientals

definitions.meaning: Massenet's opera about an Alexandrian courtesan
people from Thailand, in south-east Asia

explanation.definitionFit: Massenet's opera bears this title, and it also names the people of Thailand.

clue.text: Is it a habit of the clergy to introduce society to large quantities of alcohol?

indicators.note: to introduce one thing to another is to put it inside, so society goes into the container

parts.note: a cask is a barrel holding a large quantity of beer or wine

explanation.surface: Is getting a club drunk on barrels of drink a priestly custom?
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduce' is the container signal. 'habit' looks like a custom, but it is the clothing worn by clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A long robe worn by clergy and choristers is their garment.

clue.text: Some in observation part of carriage

indicators.note: in means the word for some is placed in the word for observation

parts.note: a comment is a remark or observation
part means some, as in part of the cake

explanation.surface: Some of the view from part of a railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'Some' looks like a quantifier for 'observation' but gives its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage is divided into separate sections for passengers.

clue.text: Try to catch trout round river, a sluggish stream

indicators.note: round means the word for trying to catch trout goes round the letter for river

parts.note: trout tickling is a way of catching fish by stroking them by hand

explanation.surface: An angler tries for trout around a slow-moving river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts TICKLE round R. Tickling is an old poacher's way of catching trout by stroking their bellies until they can be flipped out.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, slow flow of liquid is a weak stream.

clue.text: Child said to have strength

indicators.note: said means the word for child is spoken and heard as a different spelling

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A little one is reputed to be strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns MITE into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Power and force are synonyms of strength.

clue.text: Here's the rest of the cast envious over Othello

definitions.text: Here's the rest of the cast

parts.note: green with envy means envious

indicators.note: over means the word for Othello is turned back to front in this down clue

parts.note: Othello is the Moor of Venice in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: The rest of the actors are jealous of the actor playing Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses MOOR to ROOM. 'rest' looks like 'remainder', but it means a place to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors wait and relax in a backstage lounge when not on stage.

clue.text: Finally discover railway's state after landslide?

definitions.meaning: find something at last after searching
the rails are buried or out of action

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means locate after a search, and read literally describes a line put out of service.

clue.text: Crucial participant on a march collapsing before noon

indicators.note: collapsing means the letters of on a march fall apart and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A key member of the expedition collapses on the march before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' scrambles all eight letters of 'on a march', and 'before' sets the result ahead of the noon letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The key member of a team, such as the last runner in a relay, carries most responsibility.

clue.text: I care a lot about such spontaneous art

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective describing art of this kind

indicators.note: about means the letters of I care a lot are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist cares a great deal about improvised work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ICAREALOT. The answer is an adjective, so read the definition as 'describing such spontaneous art'.
explanation.definitionFit: Art or music left to chance and improvisation is described with this word from the Latin for dice.

clue.text: Made contact and begged a loan

definitions.meaning: to touch someone for money is to ask them for a loan

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both physical contact and the informal sense of tapping someone for cash.

clue.text: Delight enmeshing bishop in clerical plot

indicators.note: enmeshing means the word for delight catches the bishop inside it

parts.note: glee is delight
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is delighted to be caught in a church conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enmeshing' puts B inside GLEE. 'plot' looks like a scheme, but it is a piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Land assigned to a parish priest as part of his benefice is this.

clue.text: Stew may follow a good deal that nobody likes

definitions.text: may follow a good deal that nobody likes
definitions.meaning: in bridge, a redeal in bunches after every player has passed

explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, when all four players pass a hand, it may be followed by a special redeal of the cards in bunches, known by the name of a Hungarian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The paprika-flavoured Hungarian dish shares its name with a bridge redeal after an all-pass hand.

clue.text: One's cut out for the religious life

definitions.text: One's cut out for the religious life

parts.words: One's cut out for the religious life
parts.note: cut out for looks like suited to, but read literally it is a haircut given to monks on taking orders

explanation.surface: Someone is well suited to life as a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut out for' normally means 'well suited to', but here it is literal: the shaven crown is cut for those entering religious life.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaved patch on a monk's crown marks entry to holy orders.

clue.text: Flynn featured in character roles

indicators.note: featured in means the name is part of the words character roles, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A film star appeared in parts that called for character acting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in' shows the name inside charactER ROLes.
explanation.definitionFit: The swashbuckling Hollywood actor Flynn had this first name.

clue.text: Visionary healer is admitted to old religious devotion

indicators.note: admitted to means is gets let into the word for religious devotion

parts.note: a cult is a system of religious devotion

explanation.surface: A faith healer is accepted into an old sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted to' is the container signal. 'Visionary' looks like 'prophetic', but means to do with eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye doctor treats sight, so a healer of vision.

clue.text: Part of skeleton found in classical city

definitions.meaning: the broad upper bone of the pelvis

explanation.definitionFit: This word names both the large pelvic bone and ancient Troy.

clue.text: Oldest city father to back solid horse

indicators.note: back means the word for solid is read backwards

parts.note: a cone is a solid shape in geometry
H is slang for heroin, itself called horse

explanation.surface: A town elder supports a sturdy horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the solid shape. In Genesis he is father of Methuselah, the oldest man, and Cain named the first city after him. Horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated to its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch fathered Methuselah, the longest-lived man, and gave his name to Cain's city.

clue.text: Rushing wildly around, showing anger about incorrect map

indicators.note: about means the word for showing anger goes about the other letters

parts.note: raging means furious, showing anger

indicators.note: incorrect means the letters of map are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone storms about furiously because the map is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrect' scrambles the map letters to MPA, and 'about' places the word for showing anger around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging about violently and out of control describes a frenzy.

clue.text: Spear cut down cat in theatre

indicators.note: cut down means the vegetable is shortened, losing its front part

parts.note: a spear is a shoot of asparagus

explanation.surface: A spear is used to cut down a cat in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: In T. S. Eliot's poems and the musical Cats, the Theatre Cat is Gus, short for Asparagus, so the spear shortens to its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The elderly Theatre Cat in Eliot's poems and the musical is called this.

clue.text: This boy is a girl

parts.note: a common boy's name placed before the word boy gives the word for a boisterous girl

explanation.surface: A paradox: this lad is actually female.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the answer in front of 'boy' and you get the word for an energetic, boyish girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name that, joined to boy, makes the word for a rough-and-tumble girl.

clue.text: Poet almost had New York excited

indicators.note: excited means the letters are stirred up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A poet was nearly worked up in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' shuffles ALMOST, HAD and NY together. 'almost' looks like an instruction to drop a letter, but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh writer of Under Milk Wood, who died in New York in 1953.
